instructions: Heat a large nonstick skillet or comal over medium heat for 1 minute.
Lay 2 tortillas in the pan. Spread 1/4 cup of the cheese over each, lay a quarter of the ham on top, then 1/4 cup more cheese. Cover each with a second tortilla.

Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the bottom is golden and the cheese starts to melt. Flip them with a spatula and cook for 2 minutes, until the other side is golden and a little cheese has oozed out and browned.
Transfer them to a cutting board. Make the other 2 sincronizadas the same way with the rest of the tortillas, cheese and ham.
Cut each one into halves or quarters. Serve with the salsa.
method_notes: This takes about 12 minutes for four, not 10, because only two fit in the pan at a time. Every version is two flour tortillas filled with a melting cheese and thin ham, toasted in a dry pan on both sides. None has a rating of 4.0 or more from 20 or more people, so the lead is a fallback: Pati Jinich (5 from 3 ratings, so it has the strongest method) uses about 8 oz of cheese for 6 sincronizadas, and In Mama Maggie's Kitchen (5 from 13 ratings) uses 1/2 cup cheese and 2 slices of ham per sincronizada, which this follows. Pati Jinich allows Chihuahua, Oaxaca or Monterey Jack, and CuernaKitchen (no rating shown) names Oaxaca. Use pre-shredded cheese to keep the prep short.
